newsitem.title: FRANCE: French CIC bank profits soar before privatisation.
newsitem.headline: French CIC bank profits soar before privatisation.

text.p: France's CIC bank, which is being privatised by trade sale, said on Tuesday profits jumped 60.7 percent in the first six months of 1996 and that it expected a marked increase in profits for the year as a whole.

The regional banking group owned by state insurer GAN said it made a net attributable profit of 533 million francs ($103.3 million) in the first half of 1996 versus 332 million at the same stage in 1995.

Net banking income rose five percent to 8.562 billion francs from 8.156 billion francs but margins, which have been suffering across a depressed French banking sector for some time, declined again, however, the group said.

It said the first half was marked by a 6.7 percent advance in global lending levels and an 11.9 percent surge in commissions, notably rising GAN insurance sales commissions which accounted for 33 percent of its net banking income.

"In a still uncertain economic context, current business trends and continued productivity and risk control efforts should allow for a marked increase in the 1996 net consolidated result as a whole versus 1995, in line with expectations," the bank said in a statement.

Chairman Bernard Yoncourt said he was sticking by the terms and conditions which the government is imposing, noting that he was very attached to a "totally original" operational structure as a grouping of regional banks with nationwide coverage.

The bank has also renewed a 10-year contract with its parent to sell GAN insurance through its bank outlets, an alliance which GAN is determined to hang on to as a minority shareholder after the privatisation.
Societe Generale, Banque Nationale de Paris and the savings bank grouping Caisses d'Epargne are the most frequently cited as French suitors for CIC, otherwise known as l'Union Europeene de CIC.
The government launched a privatisation tender on August 6 and closing day for offers is October 7. GAN is selling a 67 percent stake and will keep around 25 percent.

Yoncourt told a news conference CIC's asset value including results would stand at around 14.6 billion but he was careful not to have too much read into this in terms of his position on the privatisation price.
"I'm talking about the net asset value, not the price of a transaction," he said.
The government is counting on privatising GAN itself once it the insurer bolster it finances with the sale of CIC, seen as the jewel in GAN's crown. ($1=5.158 French Franc)
